role-prior-floors.reasoning: The pipeline runs build_forecasts.py, then complete_forecasts.py, then projection_model.py. In projection_model.apply (lines 601-607), game_floor and game_ceiling start as the previous forecast's values. They are replaced only when the player has 10 or more logs in 2024-25 plus 2025-26 (own quantiles, shifted to the new rate). The calibrated game_ratios(rate) branch runs only when game_floor is None or the player has no career features. So a player with a career record but fewer than 10 recent games keeps the v3 values from complete_forecasts. For these players complete_forecasts had no earlier forecast and took the no-f branch: floor = rates[10%] and ceiling = rates[90%] of the donors' season-average rates. That is one cross-player constant, which its own gameRangeBasis calls 'NOT a calibrated game P90'. It is never shifted to the new rate. The v4 output only applies min(rate, floor) and max(rate, ceiling). The result is that 190 of the 871 v4 forecasts share gameCeiling = 17.58 exactly. 12 of them are NBA-rostered (SOURCE_REPORTED). The floors are min(previous small-sample mean, 3.83). For version 4, the card in src/main.js:237 says 'Потолок матча — 90-й процентиль собственных матчей игрока за два сезона (у новичков — игроков того же уровня)', which is false for these players. src/season.js:372 uses (gameCeiling - gameFloor)/(2*Z90) as the per-game noise in pointsSpread. On 2025-26 games the constant ceiling is not a P90: it acts as P95 for 5-7 FP/G players and P84 for 9-11 FP/G players, and 29% of games fall below the 3.83 floor. game_spread stays at about P89-P90 at every level. The defect is real but immaterial to decisions. None of the 12 are on any FBL roster (DRAFT_PICKS or live league state). They project 5.6-10.4 FP/G, far below replacement level, and cost 1000-1100 or have no Sports.ru price. The per-game SD error is about ±1.5 FP. This is a correctness/labelling bug, not an owner rule question.

injury-double-count.reasoning:
Mechanism (src/season.js:93-99, 138-145, 151-164). expectedPoints gives each future game injuryFactor (0 before the ESPN returnDate) times chainCurve(h, share), where share = playRate = clamp(forecast.games/82, .5, .97). For ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED players, forecast.games is ESPN's projected games alone (projection_model.py:586, the owner's call). When ESPN has already priced a known long absence into its total, the report zeroes those games a second time, and the already reduced season share then applies again to the games after the return.

ESPN does price old, long injuries, and the data show it. Butler 39 (ACL, back 2027-01-02), Sharpe 27 (meniscus since 08-24), DiVincenzo 4 (Achilles) and Moody 12 (patellar tendon) are impossible as healthy totals. Fresh injuries are NOT priced: Furphy (ACL diagnosed 10-19), Gueye, Strawther and Claxton have the same ESPN games in the 2026-10-17 snapshot (data/forecast-snapshots/2026-27/2026-10-17.json) as in today's 10-20 fetch (61/70/66/69). For those players the current code is correct.

So the double count is real for the priced subset only. F080's "any injured player understated 15-35%" and its critical severity are overstated. A blanket fix (share = G/gamesAfterReturn for every reported player) over-corrects fresh injuries. It would newly flag Claxton as an injured target for teams 6 and 7 (+72/+97 season), which is probably wrong. The 0.5 clamp also distorts the priced cases the other way: Moody 12 becomes 31 games, overvalued by about 200 FP.

The in-season part of F080 (playRate counts the missed games of the current spell, and then the report zeroes the rest of the spell) is only partly supported. My backtest of 160 returns from spells of 10+ games (2024/25 and 2025/26, single-club players): the code's flat playRate at the return has bias -0.099 / MAE 0.267, the spell-excluded rate +0.097 / 0.230, the prior alone +0.107 / 0.279. The chain uplift after a healthy restart is ignored here. So the code is somewhat pessimistic and the proposed exclusion over-corrects. This part is not active today (no games played yet).

Decision impact today: none of the 8 current Sports.ru rosters holds an Out player, and injuredTargets returns nothing for any team, both with the current code and with the threshold fix below. The error sits in displayed season values (transfer cards, explainSwap, injured targets) and in future decisions when a priced long-term injured player is a buy/sell candidate. This is a model calibration choice, not a league rule, so no owner decision is needed.

injury-double-count.reasoning:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced it. The auditors still overstate it today, most of their pre-season examples are wrong, and their blanket fix would do harm.

How the code works:
- chainCurve (src/season.js:104-118) solves for the hazard scale so that the chain, started healthy, plays a share `share` of 82 games. Its input should therefore be a healthy-start season share.
- expectedPoints (season.js:151-164) skips every game before the ESPN returnDate (injuryFactor=0). It then restarts that healthy chain at the return, using share=playRate.
- Any part of the reported absence already inside `share` is therefore subtracted a second time. This happens through two channels.

(1) Pre-season channel (F016/F096/F137): share = forecast.games/82, and forecast.games is ESPN's alone for ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED players (projection_model.py:587).
- Real only where ESPN's total already prices the absence. To tell which, I compared ESPN games with the model's games, scaled by the median ESPN/model ratio of the 264 ESPN players with no report (1.124).
- Priced (residual is strongly negative): long injuries known for months. DiVincenzo -66 (out 74 club games), Moody -54, Sharpe -36, Butler -10 (his model 44 already starts 'endedOut').
- Not priced (residual 0 to +29): absences reported in October. Porzingis +13, Claxton +3, Strawther +3, Gueye +3, Nurkic +13, Strus +29, Beal +16, Furphy +6 (ESPN 61 is more than the 48 games left after his return).
- So the code is right for most of the examples the auditors list. Their rule (share = G/gamesAfterReturn for every injured ESPN player) would overvalue Porzingis by about 236 FP and Claxton by about 117 FP. On today's data it also creates a spurious 'buy Claxton' injured target for teams 6 and 7.
- The pre-season double count is material for Butler (-299 FP, 25.4 vs 39.8 games) and Sharpe (-109 FP). DiVincenzo and Moody are masked by the 0.5 floor on the share (a separate issue, raised in F137).

(2) In-season channel (F080), which is larger. playRate is a per-game Beta-binomial update with k=20, and it counts every missed game of the reported spell as evidence.
- After the return the report disappears, so the whole spell keeps weighing on the post-return chain.
- ACCEPTANCE.md:98 says 'No recency weight, so the injury report is not a second penalty for a current absence'. That claim is false for long spells.
- Returns in 2024/25 and 2025/26 (213 spells of 10+ games, single-club players): the actual post-return share played was .559 / .543 / .635 for spells of 10-20 / 20-35 / 35+ games. playRate at the return gave .461 / .389 / .222, and the chain adds back only about .03-.05.
- Dropping the spell's games entirely gives .609 / .639 / .55. That is much closer but overshoots on medium spells, so the right fix sits in between: a spell should count as one event, not as N misses.

This is not an owner decision. The owner's call is 'games are ESPN's', not how a reported return is reconciled with them, and ACCEPTANCE explicitly claims the double penalty does not happen.

Why high and not critical:
- Today no FBL roster holds an Out player (only Day-To-Day players with return 10-21).
- The narrowly correct pre-season fix flips no current advice.
- The error makes the tool avoid injured players; it does not break any rule.

Why still high: in-season the bias is 25-70% of an injured player's rest-of-season value. confidence-calibration.reasoning:
Code (src/season.js:368-374, 413): confidence = Phi(gain / sqrt(sdA^2 + sdB^2)), with sd = sqrt((rel * sqrt(20/(20+played)) * points)^2 + gameSd^2 * games). rel is the pre-season season range (P10-P90 / 2.563 / meanSeason), which includes availability. The level term therefore shrinks with games played, as if the whole range were per-game rate uncertainty. Remaining-season injury and availability risk does not shrink that way. Every newcomer is also narrowed with the established rateGames=20, even though perGame uses 30 for newcomers.

(a) In-season narrowing: real, but only from about January.
- Pairs among the top 250, both players healthy. In the [.7,.8) bin, current k=20 is calibrated pre-season (.747 vs .747 month, .747 vs .756 season) and in Nov-Dec (.75 vs .73-.80).

- So the mechanism is right: remaining-season availability and role uncertainty does not shrink at sqrt(20/(20+n)).
- The repo's own inseason-calibration holdout shows the same thing: per-game MAE only falls from 2.64 to 2.03-2.19 by 30-40 games.

(b) Advised moves (selection effect): real, but it does not change decisions.
- Setup: draft-like rosters (top 80 pre-season), random pools of 15 or 40 healthy market players (ranks 81-300), best gain at least 15, season gain above 0, confidence at least .70.
- With the current rule, stated .80-.84 vs won .65-.71. Predicted gain overstates realised by about 30-40% on month (80-84 vs 47-59 FP) and about 45-55% on season (214-236 vs 104-127).
- With no narrowing, stated .77 vs won .69-.74. The gain inflation stays, because sd recalibration does not move the point estimates.
- Part of the inflation is not selection at all: even for random positive-gain pairs, the slope of realised on predicted gain is 0.74-0.91 on season.

Why I lower the severity from high to medium:
- Today (pre-season, played=0) the narrowing factor is 1, and the 70% gate is honest for the top-250 population. Over-confidence pre-season appears only above .8 (.85 vs .79-.81, .93 vs .80-.87), where the label is already 'стоит делать'.
- Advised moves still realise clearly positive gains (+47..+59 FP per month move, +104..+127 per season move). Ranking by expected gain does not depend on sd at all.
- FBL transfers are 3 per week, and league-rules.json records no carry-over. Overconfidence therefore lets through moves that are about 65% rather than 75% likely, but are still positive-EV.
- What is actually wrong is the displayed number and wording ('столько шансов'; Telegram 'забирай' at 70%), which overstate certainty by about 10 pp from January, plus overstated gain figures.

centre-bias.reasoning:
I reproduced every headline number with my own scripts, which call the repo's Veteran, examples_for and availability functions and refit nothing in the repo. The defect is real, but the deployed impact is much smaller than the "high" rating suggests, and the proposed fix is wrong if applied alone.

What is confirmed:
(1) On the 2025/26 holdout (n=484) the frozen model's centre (rate x share x 82) is biased high:
- Mean actual minus centre is -40.8 FP, with SE 14.8 (2.8 SE).
- Mean centre is 592.7 against 551.9 actual.
- Games account for -30.2 of it (games over-predicted by 2.94) and the per-game rate for -10.5.
- MAE is 249.7, which matches the report.
- The bias is negative in every forward season 2020-2026: -18.5, -48.8, -103.9, -60.4, -65.7, -59.9, -40.8.
- evaluate() reports no overall bias metric. Only healthy_start_check reports one.
(2) Survivor seasons in the share regression explain most of the games part. The regression is fitted on the last 6 targets, which include career-log seasons before 2024 that contain only catalog players. Adding a t<2024 indicator, predicted with 0, gives:
- 2026: bias -40.8 to -13.5, games bias -2.94 to -0.52, MAE 249.7 to 248.4. Dummy coefficient +0.055.
- 2025: bias -59.9 to -13.1, MAE 214.5 to 212.1.
- The Veteran class comment at lines 102-105 says age-group availability comes from the RECENT seasons. predict() never uses base_share; it uses the 6-season share_coef. The comment is inaccurate.
(3) The Ranges docstring's claim that the held-out 2025-26 season does not show the level bias is false for the statistic it removes. The 2026 median relative rate error is -0.062, inside the pool's range of -0.045 to -0.107. The median share error is about 0 in 2026 (+0.005), but it is also near 0 in several pool seasons.
(4) F070's tier pattern reproduces. Games-weighted per-game error by predicted-rate rank in 2026:
- 0-50: +0.28
- 50-100: -0.62
- 100-160: -0.98±0.45
- 160-250: -0.87±0.33
Ranks 100-250 are negative in all forward seasons 2021-2026. Minutes are over-predicted by 0.5-2.4 in the mid tier. A kernel recalibration (bandwidth 2) fitted on the 2024+2025 forward errors and applied to 2026 changes per-game MAE from 2.532 to 2.483 and season MAE from 249.7 to 246.9. That is real but modest. Missing birth dates do not explain the 2026 mid tier: only 26 test players lack one, and the tier bias is -0.78 among players who have a birth date.

What is overstated or refuted:
(a) The -41 FP is a bias of the unconditional centre, not of the deployed forecasts. The whole games over-prediction comes from the 188 players who did not play their club's opener: -14.2 games and -177 FP. For the 296 players who did play the opener:
- The unconditional model under-predicts by 4.24 games (season bias +45.7).
- With the deployed healthy shift (healthy_mean, HEALTHY_SHIFT healthy=1.0), their season bias is +0.1 FP and their games bias +0.66.
- In production, 254 of the top 313 are ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED, whose games come from ESPN. Rostered CAREER_MODEL players without an injury report get the healthy shift.
- So F068's claim that healthy-shift baselines are about 1.3 games high is not supported by the opener proxy. A residual remains: the top 160 openers by shifted centre are still -42 FP (-1.83 games, -10.6 rate).
(b) The two errors cancel. The survivor over-prediction masks a healthy-vs-unconditional gap in the chain that is too small. With the dummy alone and the shift unchanged, the openers become under-predicted by 3.37 games (+33.9 FP). Their games MAE rises from 13.36 to 13.96 and their season MAE from 249.1 to 251.4. Only a shift multiplier of about 2.0 restores the games bias (-0.04, MAE 13.39). So the fix must be joint, and its gain on the healthy branch is neutral.
(c) Replacing the U-shaped age term with a hinge (30, 35) barely moves the bias (-40.8 to -37.8) and worsens MAE in both forward seasons:
- 2026: 249.7 to 250.2
- 2025: 214.5 to 215.2
- With the dummy, 248.4 becomes 248.8.
The rise of the quadratic after about 32 is real, but it affects only a few 38+ players.
(d) The draft (18.10) is over, and the deployed build is from 20.10.

The remaining deployed effect:
- The model-side per-game over-prediction of about 0.6-1.0 FP/g in ranks 50-250. It is roughly halved for ESPN-combined players. ESPN's own bias cannot be measured.
- CAREER_MODEL players in that band (59 of the 170 at ranks 80-250, plus Duren, Zubac, Allen, Gobert and Hartenstein higher up) carry the full model bias, so they are favoured by about 0.3-0.5 FP/g against ESPN-combined peers.
- About 2.4 games too many in the unconditional games of non-healthy or unrostered CAREER_MODEL players and in the unconditionalGames field.
That is roughly 20-40 FP a season on transfer comparisons at the start of the season, when free pre-season transfers close today. This is medium severity, not high.

centre-bias.reasoning:
I reproduced the auditors' numbers exactly with my own forward refits, one model per season fitted only on earlier seasons. The documentation and reporting defects are real. The modelling impact and the proposed share-regression fix do not survive once the deployed construction is tested, not the raw model.

WHAT IS REAL
(1) The unconditional holdout centre (model rate × model share × 82) runs high in every forward season. Mean (actual − centre):
- 2020: −18.5 (SE 20)
- 2021: −48.8
- 2022: −103.9
- 2023: −60.4
- 2024: −65.7
- 2025: −59.9
- 2026: −40.8 (SE 14.8; −6.9%)
Games are about 2.9 too high on 2026.

(2) The Ranges docstring (projection_model.py:292-296) is false. It says the held-out 2025-26 season does not show the survivor level bias. In fact 2025-26 has a median relative rate error of −6.2%, the same range as the pool seasons (−4.5% to −10.7%).

(3) Two comments overstate the RECENT=3 rule:
- The Veteran class comment (lines 102-105) says age-group availability comes only from the RECENT seasons. predict() never uses base_share; it uses share_coef, which is least-squares fitted on the last 6 target seasons, survivor career-log seasons included.
- docs/ACCEPTANCE.md:116 has the same overstatement.

(4) evaluate() reports no mean-error metric at all.

(5) There is a small but consistent per-game over-prediction for ages 29-32. It is negative in 5 of 5 seasons: −1.88, −0.99, −0.05, −0.40, −0.49 FP/g (games-weighted, model only). Ranks 50-250 run about 0.3-1.2 FP/g high.

WHY IT IS IMMATERIAL FOR DECISIONS
(a) The bias sits almost entirely in players who missed their club's opener: 188 players, +14.2 games over-predicted. The 296 who played the opener are under-predicted by 4.2 games unconditionally.

(b) The deployed forecast does not use the unconditional games for healthy players. It applies the healthy-start shift (chain.healthy_mean), and the owner validated that shift in ACCEPTANCE:159. With the shift, openers have:
- games bias of −0.66
- season bias (actual − pred) of +0.1 FP on 2026
- season bias of −50, +32, +15, −44, +9 over 2022-2026, so no persistent level bias
- an age gradient whose sign flips between seasons; for example, 32+ is +131 in 2023 and −57 in 2026.
The claimed "veterans gain against young players in rankings" is therefore not a stable effect.

(c) In the deployed data, 209 of the top 250 players by per-game forecast are ESPN_MODEL_COMBINED. Their games come from ESPN, so model share bias does not reach them, and the model's rate bias is halved by the blend. In season, the prior rate is shrunk with rateGames=20, so a 0.4 FP/g prior bias is halved after about 20 games.

(d) The app ranks by meanPerGame. A monotone per-rate recalibration, as in F070, cannot reorder model-only players. The proposed share fixes leave the season ranking unchanged on 2026:
- Spearman: 0.6701 base, 0.6695 with the dummy, 0.6714 with the hinge, 0.6708 with both.
- Actual points of the top 80 by forecast: 88246, 88159, 88881, 88676. That is noise.
- Season MAE improves by only 0.5-0.8%: 249.7 to 248.4 (dummy) and to 247.8 (both).

(e) The proposed survivor dummy makes the deployed construction worse. On 2026 openers, healthy-shift games bias goes from −0.66 to −3.37 and games MAE from 13.36 to 13.96. For the top 160 openers, games MAE goes from 12.23 to 12.59. The two biases currently cancel for healthy starters: the chain's healthy shift is too weak, and the unconditional mean is too high. Fixing one without refitting the other hurts.

(f) The quadratic-to-hinge age change does nothing material: on 2026 the bias goes from −40.8 to −40.0 and MAE from 249.7 to 249.4. The 2024 dummy run is degenerate, because no complete season is in that training set.

CONCLUSION
The statistical observation is correct, but it measures a construction the app does not deploy for decision-relevant players. The claimed high severity and most impact claims are refuted. What remains is a false docstring, comments that overstate the RECENT=3 rule, and a missing bias metric in evaluate().

survival-odds.reasoning:
I reproduced the issue from scratch. My own backtest (verify2/survival/bt.mjs) builds the app's state with installDatabase(newDraft([],20000,'ON'), public/data/default-draft.json) after each of our real picks k=1,9,...,65. It reimplements the Kaplan-Meier calculation and matches plan.availabilityProfile exactly (maxdiff 0.0000).

What holds up:
(1) The survival odds are overconfident and have about zero skill where decisions are made. Skill against an in-sample constant depends on which players are scored:
- every remaining player (mostly trivial cases): +13%
- top-40 by value plus top-40 by ADP: +4%
- top-30 plus top-30: -0.4%
- top-20 plus top-20: -3.6%
The ADP half on its own is always worse than the constant. Players shown at 100% were lost 3.8% of the time. 31 of the 63 real opponent picks inside our gaps had app survival of 0.8 or more, and 10 were shown at exactly 100%. Multi-pick plan deadlines are overconfident: predicted 0.88, realised 0.76.

(2) F114, informative censoring, is real. Our own simulated pick censors a player in a way that depends on which opponent model ran, so the pooled hazard is weighted by our own choices instead of the intended 50/50. Example: Ball 0.74 pooled vs 0.50 for the 50/50 per-model average. In 9 turns, 4 estimates cross the 0.8 threshold, including two rookies. The bias runs both ways: across the top-10 by value the mean is 0.560 pooled vs 0.555 stratified. Stratifying by itself does not improve Brier (0.1112 vs 0.1086) because both component models are miscalibrated. This is a correctness fix, not an accuracy gain.

(3) F125/F143 hold. 373 of the 494 ESPN ADPs sit in [130,142) and take only 45 distinct values, so that block is a censored cluster, not a ranking. Rookies outside the top 5 sit at ADP 126-140. adpDraft adds noise with sd ≈ 1.5+0.2*ADP ≈ 29 to that cluster.

(4) F126 holds. adpDraft has no rookie reservation and threw in 1 of 25 ADP runs at k=17, 33 and 41 and in 3 of 25 at k=57; the bot model never failed. planAdvice (plan.js:111,121) returns the requested runs, not profile.runs. The UI (main.js:328) also says all opponents are the app's bots, when half are ADP-noise humans.

What is overstated:
- The GM never saw these numbers during the 18.10 draft. The KM censoring and the 'calibrated bots' arrived in #40 on 19.10, and the repo is a shallow clone that starts on 19.10.
- The backtest flatters the model. observedRookieRounds draws the bots' rookie habits from this same DRAFT_PICKS, and the valuation postdates the draft. It is also only one draft with correlated events.
- The take-now decision itself looks roughly calibrated: planned next-pick players were predicted at 0.906 and 0.875 survived (8 entries).
- ACCEPTANCE.md makes no calibration claim for survival.

So the defect is real, but it only affects training mode until the next draft in October 2027. I lowered the severity from high to medium. The fitted conditional-logit replacement (F124) is a plausible improvement, but its evidence is one draft, so I did not verify it as necessary.

injury-feed-outage.reasoning:
I checked the code path at f5c0328. When ESPN fails, `espn_injuries()` (scripts/collect_sports_current.py:252-258) returns None. This covers any fetch error after `fetch()`'s 3 retries, and a 404 too, because `fetch` returns None and `json.loads(None)` raises inside the try. `main()` sets `out['espnInjuries']` only when that result is truthy (lines 575, 582-583). It never falls back to `previous['espnInjuries']`, even though `previous` is already loaded from OUT, which season_watch fills with a copy of the live snapshot. `season_watch.merge_full` (season_watch.py:42-56) carries over journals and missing players but not espnInjuries. The collection still counts as ok, so `notify()` runs at once. The snapshot then stays injury-less until the next full collection, 120 minutes later (`--full-every 120`), and every journal change in that window runs the notifier on it.

In the notifier, `ctx.injuries=parseInjuries(live.espnInjuries)` (notify-transfers.mjs:28) becomes an empty Map, and nothing warns about it. The UI is different: season-ui.js:68-72 fetches ESPN directly, then uses the snapshot, then shows 'Отчёт ESPN о травмах недоступен'. In the notifier:
- `targets=injuredTargets(...)` comes back empty, so the 'soon' messages stop.
- The 'back' block (line 147) treats every id in `previous.watch` that has no injury entry as returned. It posts '✅ X вернулся в строй' with 'забирай' or 'можно брать'.
- `state.watch` is then reset to [], so this happens once per outage per watched target.
- The `hurt` list empties. If a 'changed' message goes out, `state.injuries` is overwritten with [], and on recovery the same roster injuries are reported again as new.
- marketAlerts, bestPackage, acquisition and transferVerdict all value injured players as healthy.

The defect is reachable, not handled, and not documented as intended. Frequency is the only moderator: it needs all 3 ESPN attempts to fail on the 2-hourly fetch. Medium is justified because the alert can tell the owner to spend one of his 3 weekly FBL transfers on a player who is still out. With the current data the deal for Harris happens to stay 'worth' either way. But a long-out target in the watch list would pass the default month floor only because the injury is missing.

nba-cup-80-games.reasoning:
Both parts of the claim reproduce on the current data, but neither changes a decision, so this is low rather than the claimed medium.

(1) NBA Cup games. Each of the 30 clubs in live-sports-current.json has 80 calendar games, ending 2027-04-12. Week 8 (05.12–14.12 MSK) holds only 28 club-games. That is the Cup knockout window where the 2 TBD games will go. The 2 TBD games are real FBL games: the quarterfinal and semifinal count as regular season, and so do the replacement games for clubs that do not advance. Every club ends at 82 counted games, and the Yahoo scoring window covers them.

The code builds the share from 82 games. playRate takes its prior as forecast.games/82, and chainCurve is calibrated on 82 games (src/season.js:91-117). But expectedPoints (season.js:151-170) only sums the club's calendar games that are still ahead, and there are 80. So every season-horizon number is 80/82 of the forecast. This shows up in three places: the standings 'Прогноз сезона', the Teams tab's season window, and gain.season.

The collector re-reads calendars on every season-data run, so the gap closes by itself once Sports.ru publishes the games in early December. The 2 games are missing for every club in the same week, so the scaling is almost uniform. Team order and the sign of transfer gains do not change. The impact is the absolute numbers, which are biased now and will jump in December.

(2) The standings forecast counts no transfers. In season-ui.js:137, rest = sum of playerOutlook().season.points over the current 10 players. Every game a player is expected to miss counts as 0 points for the slot. The draft tab does the opposite. scenarioSeasonScore and slotSeason add forecast.transfer.value. ACCEPTANCE.md:164-165 says a long absence costs a team only until the player is replaced, and the project's own backtest shows slot value predicts better (slot MAE 186 vs 323). So the same rosters get two different season forecasts and different mid-table orders. The UI does not say the standings forecast assumes no transfers. The standings are display only and no transfer decision reads them.

A team forecast is not a league rule, so the owner does not need to decide. The fix is to add the replacement value, or at least label the column.

Separate bug noticed during the repro, outside this issue: chainCurve with hazards [0,0] returns an availability of 1.0 for every game, whatever the share. This affects 5 players: Knueppel, Podziemski, Mikal Bridges, Julian Champagnie and Bub Carrington. Each gets 80/80 games, against about 76 from their share. It should go into its own finding.

playrate-clamp.reasoning:
The defect is real, but it does not change any advice today, so I rate it medium, not the claimed high.

Mechanism (src/season.js:94): playRate sets prior = Math.min(.97, Math.max(.5, forecast.games/82)), with weight CALIBRATION.availability.priorGames = 20 team games. expectedPoints then scales chainCurve so the chain's 82-game mean equals that share, or uses the flat share for players without hazards. Any forecast under 41 games is therefore treated as about 41 games.

The clamp was copied from scripts/inseason_calibration.py:68. There the prior is the raw previous-season games count, and only players with 20+ games and 10+ minutes per game qualify (prior_of). In production, forecast.games is already a fitted forecast: the regression, or its mean with ESPN, or the rookie models. docs/ACCEPTANCE.md also says "the hazards are scaled so the chain's mean equals the forecast games", and the floor contradicts that for every forecast under 41 games. Nothing documents the floor as intended, and the tests only use 78- and 82-game forecasts.

journal-short-names.reasoning: I reproduced the mechanism, but nothing shows the trigger can happen. Journal events are keyed by (date, side, name, price). If a short name changes for the same deal, an old event of that date disappears, so stamp_journal.keep() returns None and follow() can no longer match the renamed events. Those rows get seenAt=now and lose any sid pins, because pin() only finds players who left or joined the roster since the last read. journalTransfers then compares the journal name against shortName(), which prefers the static database sportsName over the live roster name. The renamed rows do not resolve and are dropped with warnings. The trigger itself is unconfirmed. Today there are 0 name mismatches, the journal has 18 rows and no pager, and we do not know whether Sports.ru re-renders old journal rows when it changes a short name. It does use initials to tell namesakes apart ('Э. Мобли'). The protocol guard ('На проверке' when the replay roster differs from Sports.ru) does not always catch it: in the reproduced case the two dropped deals cancel out, so the replayed roster equals the real one and the drop is silent.

verdict-band.reasoning:
transferVerdict (src/season.js:312-323) labels a transfer that has already been made by comparing its expected month and season gains with a fixed T=15 FP. It never looks at uncertainty. The confidence machinery in the same file (pointsSpread/explainSwap, plus CONFIDENT=.7 and DOUBTFUL=.6 at line 365) is used for advice but not here. On current data, one swap has a season SD of 439-775 FP and a month SD of 85-148 FP. A ±15 band is therefore about ±0.03 SD on the season, so 'even' almost never fires (0 of 20 real transfers) and coin-flip moves get firm labels. Examples: 'LeBron James > Anthony Davis' gets '💪 Усиление' at P(gain>0) 58% season and 59% month. 'Tyler Herro > Onyeka Okongwu' gets '🤡 Ослабление' at 54% and 56% against. 'Isaiah Hartenstein > Egor Demin' gets 'Ослабление' with a season gain of -1 FP (50%). Only 7 of 20 labels reach the tool's own 70% CONFIDENT level on the season horizon, and 6 of 20 are below 60%. The advice engine would call the same move 'сомнительно', so the two outputs contradict each other.

Why low and not high: the labels appear only in the owner's private Telegram notifier (rival-transfer and own-transfer messages). transferVerdict is not imported by the UI or by league-feed. The numeric gains are printed next to the label. The actionable 'Тебе: …' advice in the same message is already gated by explainSwap confidence (CONFIDENT/DOUBTFUL), so no transfer decision or FP depends on the verdict. Its expected-value direction is not wrong either: a +139 FP expectation is an upgrade in expectation. The defect is a misleading certainty in commentary, not a wrong decision.

Side claims:
- 'Spreads are not calibrated as the docs claim': refuted as stated. ACCEPTANCE.md lines 119/147/156 openly report 72-74% coverage of the 80% range. That is a separate calibration topic, not part of this fix.
- 'Game noise dominates a one-week horizon' (pointsSpread comment): measured median game-noise variance share is 0.50 (IQR 0.42-0.60) on today's week horizon. The comment overstates it, but the share grows as in-season games shrink the prior term, so this is immaterial.

verdict-band.reasoning:
The arithmetic is right: ±15 FP is small next to the swap SD from explainSwap. The finding's conclusion does not follow from it, and the fix it proposes is worse than the current code.

1) What the label says. transferVerdict (src/season.js:312-323) gives the sign of the expected gain. It compares playerOutlook means over 4 weeks and over the season, and uses ±15 FP as the house threshold for a material change; acquisition and marketAlerts use the same 15 as minGain. This is the documented design: ACCEPTANCE.md:111 says "a season gain decides a verdict first", an injured player bought for the season is "a season investment", and tests/season.test.js:187-195 locks this in ('down' for a 30→20 FP/game swap, 'even' for 30→31). FBL standings are total FBL points, and points add up. So for "did this move make their team stronger in expectation?", the expected gain is the right quantity. Telegram always prints the magnitude beside the label (notify-transfers.mjs:113/124 + telegram-format gains()), for example "📈 Им: +139 ФО за сезон · +32 за 4 нед. · 💪 Усиление". For the owner's own moves it is also prefixed "По модели".

2) The wrong yardstick. explainSwap.confidence is P(realised gain > 0) under the full spread of outcomes: the calibrated season range, which includes injuries and games missed, plus game-to-game noise. That is outcome risk, not the chance that "stronger in expectation" is wrong. My decomposition shows game noise is only about 5% of season variance. With game noise alone, every |s| ≥ 124 move has P ≥ 0.88. The 0.55-0.65 values therefore come from the season-range term, which is mostly availability and injury risk that cannot be known in advance. A label about expected value should not be rewritten into one about outcome probability. "The even band is hit 2-3% of the time" is likewise the chance that a realised outcome lands within ±15. The verdict never uses that quantity.

3) The proposed fix does harm. Gating on P_season ≥ 0.70 / ≤ 0.30 on the current data turns 13 of the 20 real transfers into "🤷 Примерно равноценно". Ten of them have |season gain| ≥ 124, including Embiid>Kawhi +285, Buzelis>LeBron +238/+80, Knueppel>Okongwu −209 and White>Knueppel +207. Calling those "roughly equal" is a false statement about expected value. It would hide exactly the rival threats the finding wants to show. The 0.25·sd band also relabels LeBron>AD (+139/+32) as "even".

4) The threshold does not matter in practice. With today's live snapshot all 20 labels are directional (10 up, 10 down). A much coarser ±50 season / ±25 month band changes only 3: Embiid>Kawhi and George>Edey move from up to long because their month gain is exactly +25, and Fox>Pritchard (−41/−23) moves from down to even.

5) It drives no decision. The label is used only in the two notifier messages. Whether to grab the player a rival released is decided by decide(), which has its own CONFIDENT=0.7 gate and says "🤔 можно взять, но не уверенно" below it. That fits "upgrade in expectation, uncertain" and does not contradict it.

6) The side claims are overstated or wrong:
- (a) Calibration: holdout coverage80 is 0.746 (projection-report-only.json) and 0.740 (projection-model-audit.json). That implies an SD factor of 1.12-1.14, not 1.19; the 72% figure is the older ACCEPTANCE.md:119 line. ACCEPTANCE reports the shortfall openly (lines 119/147/156), and the misses are asymmetric (above 15%, below 11%). Verdicts do not use the SD at all, so no label can change.
- (b) "Game noise dominates a one-week horizon is false": game noise is a median 56% of week variance (p10 0.32, p90 0.75), and over 50% for 62% of 456 players. The comment holds.

What is left is presentation only: the label shows no confidence, and the same absolute 15 FP applies to 4 weeks (about 1 FP/game) and the season (about 0.2 FP/game). That is an optional UX tweak (for example appending the season %), not a math error or a defect.

objective-pfirst.reasoning:
The math in the cluster holds up. What it means for decisions today is much smaller than the auditors claimed, and the objective itself is a league-owner choice, not a code defect.

1. Code confirms the objective. The draft scores players with riskAdjustedValue = slotSeason/82 - 0.14*(mean - floor)/82 (src/valuation.js:32-37, 'balanced' style). That feeds plan.js:66, the bots (simulation.js:37), main.js:296 and insights.js:8, which Telegram uses through notify-transfers.mjs:65. The season optimiser bestPackage (src/season.js:268-318) maximises expected playerOutlook points and has no variance or rank term. The season tab shows the place as a point estimate only (src/season-ui.js:413-414).

2. Variance really does raise P(1st), for every team. I used the app's own sampler (scenarioSeasonScore) on the real 80-pick rosters with common random numbers over 60k runs. I compared adding zero-mean noise of sd 500 (team sd +82..94) against adding +100 FP of mean. One FP of team sd is worth 0.48 / 1.04 / 1.00 / 0.60 / 1.37 / 1.57 / 1.31 / 1.04 FP of mean for teams 1..8. This matches F113's 0.48-1.43. So a downside penalty applied to everyone has the wrong sign if the prize is 1st place. The 'balanced' penalty is 50/74/103 FP (p10/p50/p90) over the top 120 players.

3. Why the impact is small now:
- (a) The draft ended on 18.10. DRAFT_PICKS has 80 entries and the app's draft state was complete. So the plan, the ФО* column, the alternatives and the bots no longer drive a real decision. Their only live use is the 'value per 1000' pros/cons text in cards and Telegram.

4. F036 (no P(place) on the season tab) is true. objective-pfirst.reasoning:
The math in the findings is right in direction but too narrow. On current data, team variance does raise P(1st) for all 8 teams. Calling the draft penalty a "math-error" (F113, high) does not hold up, for four reasons.

(1) The penalty is a documented design choice, not an accident. src/valuation.js:32-33 says "A style only states a preference about the downside", docs/SCORING_AUDIT.md:52 says the same, and main.js:328 tells the user that the plan's ФО are "с поправкой на риск". The UI does not hide it.

(2) The sign of the "correct" risk preference depends on the prize structure, and that structure is not recorded anywhere: league-rules.json, ACCEPTANCE and the docs have no prize or payout fields. On the current post-draft rosters, using the app's own sampler (scenarioSeasonScore, 60k common-random-number draws), the value of 1 FP of team sd in FP of mean is:
- P(1st) objective: +0.42 for the owner's team 0, the favourite.
- Top-3 objective: -0.35 for team 0.
- Expected place: -0.38 for team 0.
- Weaker teams: positive under every objective.
So for the user's own team the downside penalty fits expected place and top-3, and goes the wrong way only if just 1st place counts. The claim that "no rank-based objective supports the penalty" is false for the team the app advises.

(3) The magnitude is small. The penalty is a median 5.3% of slot value (p10-p90 3.9-7.7%) in the top 120. It reorders 28% of near-neighbour pairs, but only where raw gaps are 43 FP or less, so near-ties only. The auditor's own replay found the now-pick identical under balanced and risk-neutral at 10 of 10 picks.

(4) The draft finished on 18.10.2026, so plan.js and the MILP no longer drive any 2026/27 decision. The season optimizer (bestPackage, recommendation) is already risk-neutral on expected FP, with a season-not-lowered constraint. The Telegram 'value per 1000' cue uses riskAdjustedValue, but a near-proportional 5% shift barely moves its percentiles.

The in-season angle (F029) is real but objective-dependent too. A swap from median to p90 player spread (sd 401 to 558) changes team sd by about 59 FP, worth about ±25 FP for team 0 depending on the objective. Swaps at the extremes are worth about ±35 FP. This matters mostly late in the season, and the static model ignores the 75 future transfers each team has.

F036 (no P(place) in the season tab) is a feature request. It also runs against a documented stance: SCORING_AUDIT.md:3 says random first-place shares were deliberately removed from primary recommendations, and ACCEPTANCE:20/53/61 says model first-place shares are not win probabilities. The deterministic table is not wrong. "Прогноз" is a point forecast, and the top two (28.0% vs 24.3% P1 on current data) are indeed close.

F123 is a wording nit. The Wilson interval correctly measures Monte-Carlo error of the model's share. The note under the table already says it is not a win probability, but the tooltip "95% доверительный интервал" can be misread as uncertainty about winning.

Overall the issue is real as an improvement and a disclosure point, immaterial to current decisions, and its core depends on an owner decision.

missing-birthdates.reasoning:
The data defect is real and the counts match exactly. data/career-players.json has 222 of 885 people with birthDate null; 221 of the 805 players in the history have no age. All 222 have an nbaId and 213 have an espnId, so the gap can be filled. The missing dates are not random. extract_career_games.py takes birthDate from the provider_identities table, and that table seems to hold ESPN athlete records only for catalog players. So in every season 2018-2026, only 1 of the age-missing transitions is a current player (Fred VanVleet); the rest are players who later left the league.

Code path, checked against scripts/projection_model.py. History.age returns None. predict() then adds no age_pm or age_min term (b is None). share_features falls back to age 27 through `x['age'] or 27`. _age_curve and base_share skip these rows. So the RECENT-window age curves are fitted only on players who stayed in the league, which is the survivor selection that window was meant to avoid. In the share-regression window, 623 of 2,474 rows carry the fake age 27; that number reproduces exactly.

The effect is real but smaller than the auditor implies. With debut-based imputation in the fit (my own reproduction), the production model's per-game forecast for the 441 current players with known age falls by 0.215 FP/g on average. The fall is broad across ages, not limited to veterans: 0-25 -0.165, 25-28 -0.295, 34+ -0.219. Ages 34+ also lose 0.044 share, about -61 FP per season in the model. Games come from ESPN only and the per-game rate is a 50/50 blend with ESPN for 300 players, so the published shift is -0.142 FP/g on average (-0.109 for ESPN-blended players) and -7.9 FP per season (under 1%). Published rankings barely move: in the top 80 the mean move is 0.68 places, the largest is 8, and 79 of 80 stay in the top 80. FVV, a current player with no age, is the clearest individual error: the model gives 13.57 FP/g with no age term against 12.51 at an imputed 31.7, so the published figure is about +0.53 FP/g, or 957 vs 921 season FP (rank 117 vs 125).

Forward tests, known-age players only, 2024/2025/2026:
- Unweighted per-game MAE improves every season: 2.336->2.306, 2.242->2.158, 2.641->2.604.
- Games-weighted per-game MAE is mixed: +0.011, -0.048, +0.001.
- Season MAE barely changes: +0.3, -1.1, -1.8 FP.
- Games-weighted per-game bias goes from +0.18/+0.41/+0.17 to -0.23/-0.03/-0.18: the over-forecast goes away, but in 2024 and 2026 it overshoots into an under-forecast.

The claimed holdout effect is mostly not about age. The 26 age-missing test players in 2026 do over-forecast by 302 FP, which is 16 of the 41 FP mean bias. Imputing their age only brings that to 295, because they are players about to leave the league, and no age can capture that.

Conclusion: a real data error with a confirmed, consistent upward bias in the model component of about 0.2 FP/g (about 0.1-0.14 published), plus a clear mispricing of FVV. Accuracy and ranking gains are small, and the draft has already happened, so medium severity, not high.

missing-birthdates.reasoning:
The facts are right. data/career-players.json has 222 of 885 people with birthDate null. load() (projection_model.py:498) drops them, so History.age gives None for those players. Three things follow:
- Veteran._age_curve skips their rows.
- predict() adds no age term for them.
- share_features puts in age 27.
In the production age-curve window (targets 2024-26), 260 of 1,405 played transitions have no age (8% of the minute weight). In the share regression, 623 of 2,474 rows do. The data are missing not at random: the gaps are mostly players who later left the league, and they declined. Dropping them is a look-ahead survivor selection, so the auditor has the direction right. No owner decision or ACCEPTANCE item covers ages.

The size and the framing do not hold up for this league.

1) It is a level shift, not an age effect. I refitted the production Veteran model with imputed ages: median age 21.46 at the first season, plus elapsed years. The model rate of the 441 current players with known ages fell by 0.229 FP/g on average. The fall was biggest for the youngest group:

|---|---|
| 18-25 | -0.253 |
| 25-29 | -0.224 |
| 29-33 | -0.226 |
| 33+ | -0.164 |

So "veterans pushed up" against younger players is wrong. The only relative effect is non-rookies against the separate rookie model, by about 0.15 FP/g after the ESPN blend.

2) Rankings do not change. Across the 418 priced players, the published per-game change is -0.148 on average (sd 0.085). The top 40/80/120/200 by forecast keep 39/40, 79/80, 119/120 and 200/200 of the same players, and no top-150 player moves more than 7 places. Season totals drop 8 FP on average (sd 9). For the top 100 that is 10.6 FP out of 1,326 (0.8%). In an 8-team league decided by relative choices, this is noise next to the about 2.4 FP/g MAE of a single forecast.

3) Forward tests show a calibration gain only, with no gain in accuracy. On known-age players, frozen fits with targets before T:

|---|---|---|---|

| T=2026 | 2.424 → 2.430 | +0.17 → -0.20 | 238.3 → 237.4 |

The over-prediction is real and imputing removes it. Accuracy is unchanged.

- Yang Hansen: a fringe player at 3.8 FP/g.

Against rookies the shift is about 0.15 FP/g, far below forecast noise. One free agent is off by more: VanVleet (1600, not owned in FBL) is about 0.4-0.6 FP/g (3-4%) too high. The draft is complete, so no draft decision was affected; in-season transfer comparisons change by amounts inside the uncertainty. Holdout bias reporting is inflated: season bias +28 vs +7 FP (2026).
missing-birthdates.fixPlan:
1) In scripts/projection_model.py, give History a fallback for players without a birth date instead of returning None. In load(), compute A0 = the median of History.age(pid, first[pid]) over known-birth players whose first season is after 2004 (about 21.5). In History.age, when births has no entry and pid is in self.first, return A0 + (year - self.first[pid]). A better option where data/official-nba-player-index.json has DRAFT_YEAR: use 21.1 + (year - (DRAFT_YEAR+1)). Mark these with x['ageImputed']=True in features(), so the report can count them. With this, _age_curve, predict() and share_features all see an age, and the silent fill of 27 never triggers for NBA players.
2) Data: when the history checkpoint is next refreshed, fill birthDate from provider_identities or ESPN athlete for the 222 nulls. At minimum, add the current-pool players Fred VanVleet (1994-02-25) and Yang Hansen (2005-06-26) to data/career-players.json, so default-draft also shows their age.
3) Regenerate the forecast through the normal pipeline (not in this audit).

espn-parser-missing-stat.reasoning: The bug is real. In scripts/espn_context.py:15, individual_projection() returns None if any of 12 stat keys is missing (`not finite(stats.get(key))`). ESPN leaves out a stat whose projected season total is 0. Non-shooting centers have no '17' (3PM) and a few wings have no '1' (blocks), so their whole projection is thrown away even though it is internally consistent. build_forecasts.py:93-98 then never marks them ESPN_INDIVIDUAL, and projection_model.py:581-587 sets espn=None. Their per-game value becomes the career model alone (no equal-weight ESPN blend, which ACCEPTANCE.md:121 promises) and their games come from the model chain. That breaks the owner's explicit rule from PR #61 (22a494a): "games are ESPN's whenever ESPN projects the player, the model's only when it does not". These players do have an ESPN game projection (espnContext.projectedGames is set), so the deviation is not intended. The points identity check (PTS = 2*FGM + 3PM + FTM) already guards against a 3PM that is missing but really nonzero, so treating an omitted optional stat as 0 is safe. The effect is material: 5 drafted starters (Zubac, Gobert, Allen, Duren, Hartenstein) get season forecasts 170-340 FP too low, and today's live transfer advice changes. I rate it high rather than critical: nothing crashes and no league rule is broken, but the forecasts are wrong and change decisions, and the C position is biased downward as a group. No owner decision is needed, because the owner already ruled that ESPN games apply to every player ESPN projects.

espn-parser-missing-stat.reasoning:
Root cause. scripts/espn_context.py:15 individual_projection() returns None when any of the 12 stat keys is missing (`not finite(stats.get(key))`). ESPN's kona_player_info leaves out a stat whose projected value is 0. Three things show this. (a) My own read-only GET shows Gobert and Poeltl have no key '17', while Jokic, LeVert and Stewart have it. (b) Among the 313 players who parse today, none has 3PM or BLK exactly 0 (the smallest 3PM is 0.014/g), so every exact-zero record is being dropped. (c) With the missing keys set to 0, all 24 records pass the parser's own checks: PTS=2FGM+3PM+FTM, makes<=attempts, minutes/G<=48.

Downstream. build_forecasts gives these players HISTORICAL_BASELINE instead of ESPN_INDIVIDUAL. projection_model.apply (line 581) then sets espn=None, so games=model_games and rate=model_rate. That contradicts the claimed method: ACCEPTANCE line 67 says "the source game projection overrides the historical availability weight when present", line 121 gives the ESPN/model mean, and the code comment says "Games are ESPN's alone (the owner's call)". This is not an owner decision to exclude these players. Line 78 ("never zero-filled") concerns missing forecasts, not ESPN's omitted zero stats.

The bias is systematic, not noise. On covered players the model averages 58.5 games against ESPN's 67.4. On the 24 affected players it is 55.6 against 63.6. So mostly non-shooting centers lose about 8-9 games (about 13% of season value) compared with the rule every other player gets.

Magnitude holds on current data. My independent re-estimate (ESPN full per game = component + a bigs-fitted PF/participation offset, sd 0.49) matches the auditor within about 25 FP: Lively +510, Zubac 1086->1425, Allen 1170->1478, Poeltl +287, M.Robinson +237, Gobert +219, Hartenstein +217, Duren +169, Mark Williams 925->431.

Decision impact is real. With the current live snapshot, bestTransfers(sort=season) recommends T4 "Zubac->Vucevic +155" and "Gobert->Vucevic +96", and T5 "Allen->Vucevic +73". All three vanish under the fix (month sort: T4 "Gobert->Alex Sarr +13" and T5 "Allen->Embiid +17" also vanish). This happens during today's free pre-season transfer window, which closes 20.10 21:30 MSK.

I downgraded from critical to high: there is no rule violation and no illegal roster. The cause is a forecast/advice bias of about 100-500 season FP per affected player (about 1-4% of a team's season total), touching 4 rostered starters on 2 teams. No owner decision is needed: ESPN's zero-omission is an API fact, the points identity proves 3PM=0, and the house rule already says to use ESPN games when present. One caveat: the frozen 17 October ESPN snapshot (pack_online_evidence) also lacks these 24, so measuring ESPN accuracy later will under-represent centers unless they are added.

transfer-hours-advice.reasoning:
Both parts of F010 hold up when checked against the code and the live data.

(1) The transfer hours are not in the advice path. TRANSFER_HOURS is used only in rules.js, which judges transfers already made (transferTime / checkRules 'time'), and in the season-ui.js rules list (line 590). The advice code never reads the clock. recommendation(), takeAction(), packageCard() and optionRow() get only ctx.today, a Moscow date, so the card shows "Сделай этот трансфер" with a primary "Сделать на Sports.ru ↗" link or a "Записать" button at any hour. notify-transfers.mjs never imports TRANSFER_HOURS or reads the time. Its "🎯 Тебе: забирай", "🤔 можно взять", "🧩 Лучший ход", "✅ вернулся в строй — забирай" and "🔜 можно брать" messages carry no "с 08:00" note.

The watcher (season_watch.py, chained six-hour runs) calls notify() after every full collection, every 2 hours around the clock, and after every journal change. Games end around 04:00-08:00 MSK and ESPN injury news lands around 00:00-02:00 MSK, so this advice will often arrive outside the hours. Sports.ru does not enforce the FBL hours, which is why the league feed exists. A move made at night is therefore a certain breach: transferTime gives 'breach', checkRules sets certain:true, and the league feed posts a public protocol with Зак Онн and the commissioner tagged (ACCEPTANCE.md line 181).

There is one mitigation: the rules list shows "Трансферы только с 08:00 до 22:00 МСК", and the owner set this rule today. So a breach needs the user to act on the advice against a rule he knows. Still, the advice itself is time-blind. The week's last window has the same gap: from Sunday 22:00 to 24:00 the transfers KPI and the recommendation still offer the expiring week's transfers, which can no longer be used.

(2) The 'week' horizon is empty every Monday. horizons().week.to = weekOf(today, gameWeeks).end, the end of the Sports.ru tour, a Monday in Moscow dates (week 1 is 20.10-26.10, week 2 is 27.10-02.11). Monday-dated games are Sunday-evening US games and are over by about 08:00 MSK. So for the whole Monday transfer window the horizon holds 0 games, exactly when the FBL week resets to 3 fresh transfers. Meanwhile transferWeek() in season.js already counts a move on a tour's last day toward the next tour.

Scoring is Yahoo rotisserie season totals (league-rules.json yahoo.scoringType), so the 'week' lens is only for planning. The default horizon is 'month', and the notifier uses month/season. So the second part is low impact: wrong "hold" advice on Mondays only for users who chose «Неделя». The finding's wording "the transfer budget ends Sunday 22:00" is correct per fblWeek plus the hours. The rule itself is decided, so this needs no owner decision.

gain-split-zero.reasoning:
The finding is real. In src/season.js (lines 386-391 at f5c0328), splitProduct returns [total,0,0] whenever any factor is <= 0. explainSwap feeds it [perGame, expectedGames/clubGames, clubGames] for each side, so the whole gain lands in parts.perGame in two cases:
- a side has expectedGames=0 (an injured player out for the whole horizon);
- a side has clubGames=0 (its club has no games left in the week horizon).

parts is shown in two places: the "Почему и об игроках" line in src/season-ui.js:316 (single swaps, packages and the best-pick card) and the Telegram line "Откуда: … ФО/матч · … доля матчей · … календарь" in scripts/notify-transfers.mjs:50. parts also drives the two flags in explainSwap, ">half from availability" and ">half from schedule", and both are silently turned off in exactly these cases.

Not affected: gain, sd, confidence, level and the ranking or advice logic. Only the explanation text and the two warning flags are wrong.

On today's data (20.10, the season starts tonight) no rostered player hits the case: none of the 6 injured rostered players has 0 expected games, and none of the 1514 UI top-10 options checked used the fallback. In season the case is routine:
- selling an injured player is a main use of the tool;
- on the last day of a week (26.10), 258 of 482 market players have no club games left in the week horizon.

The docs claim (docs/ACCEPTANCE.md:141, the gain is "split exactly (logarithmic mean)") holds only for positive factors. Nothing here is a league-rule question.

myopic-policy.reasoning:
Code facts (f5c0328). explainSwap gives confidence = Phi(gain/sd) with CONFIDENT=.7 and DOUBTFUL=.6 (src/season.js:362-417). marketAlerts (season.js:355-357) keeps a swap only if month gain >= minGain (20 at every call site), season gain > 0 and confidence >= 0.7. That gate drives the app's "Для тебя" alerts and the "Рекомендуем" chip (season-ui.js:222, 474). It also drives the Telegram "Отдельные усиления" list, whether a Telegram message gets sent at all (notify-transfers.mjs:44), and "забирай" versus "можно взять, но не уверенно" (notify-transfers.mjs:98-100). The app's main recommendation (season-ui.js:432-441) only rejects DOUBTFUL moves, so it already uses a 60% gate. transferVerdict's "season decides first" only labels transfers after they happen, and does not choose moves. acquisition() needs season gain >= 15 and month gain >= 0, and only runs for a player a rival released or for injured targets. The 70% rule is written up in docs/ACCEPTANCE.md (19 Oct) as the developer's design. No league-owner decision about it appears in data/league-rules.json.

Claim checked: a 70% gate is a hidden higher EV threshold, because P >= 0.7 means gain >= 0.524*sd. On the current deployed data (today 2026-10-21, all 8 teams, top-10 single swaps) the median pair sd over the month horizon is 108 FP. The 70% gate therefore needs about 56 FP of month gain, against the nominal minGain of 20. Of 17 options with gain >= 20 and season > 0, only 2 pass 70%, while 15 pass 60%. So the gate does dominate the alert logic. The sd shrinks as games of this season arrive.

I built my own replay of 2025/26 (433 players, 164 days, Mon-Sun weeks, 3 non-rolling transfers, same-position swaps). The predictor is a shrunk rate x availability x club games, with the remaining absence taken from 2024/25 spell lengths. sd uses the tool's formula. Here the effective 70% threshold came out at about 30-40 FP, so the replay is if anything milder than the live tool. Result: the 70% gate does lose value against the same rule without it, or against the app's 60% rule, in most scenarios. The size is about 35-115 FP a season (0.3-0.9% of a ~13,000-14,800 team total), and in one realistic scenario it is zero within noise. That is well below the auditor's -128 to -164.

The auditor's proposed fix is a Bellman shadow price, i.e. lambda = 0 on the last day of the week. It is not robustly better. With rivals contesting free agents and no cap, every "Sunday" variant came out worse than the plain 70% rule (-38 to -83, se about 50). The direction (EV over a high-confidence gate) is real but modest and depends on the scenario. The app's main recommendation is unaffected. The large magnitude and the option-value machinery are not reproduced. Hence PLAUSIBLE, low.

arrival-missed-games.reasoning:
The mechanism is real. In src/season.js:93-99, playRate sets team=max(rows, finished, on). `finished` counts every scored game of the player's current Sports.ru club since opening night, so club games played before a trade or signing count as missed. This is intended and documented, though. docs/ACCEPTANCE.md:98 says "counted against the club calendar too", and tests/season.test.js:78 asserts it. The real question is whether it hurts the forecast, so I backtested it on the 2025-26 logs (appearances only, prior = 2024-25 games/82 clipped to [.5,.97], or the runtime's .85 default when a player has no prior, k=20). The target was the share of the club's remaining games the player actually played.

F041, traded players (n=64-67): the current formula A is slightly better than the proposed own-team-games formula B. At t=10, MAE is 0.266 for A against 0.276 for B, bias is +0.068 against +0.090, and the error in rest-of-season games is +1.7 against +2.1. The gap is negligible, and A is closer.

F086, late arrivals at a new club or with no prior (signings, call-ups, 10-day players; n=43-73): they really play only about 31-35% of the remaining club games. The current formula is almost unbiased (share bias -0.07 to +0.005; games bias +0.1 to +1.1). The proposed arrival-based fix over-forecasts by +0.20 to +0.34 of share, which is +7 to +12 games. It still over-forecasts by +0.43 among players averaging 20+ minutes. For players with no prior, whose 0.85 default matches the runtime exactly, A is off by +0.005 and B by +0.378. Counting the pre-arrival games works as useful shrinkage for fringe arrivals. The auditor's synthetic case assumes a signing who then plays every game, and the data says they don't. The proposed fix would make transfer advice worse, so F041 and F086 are REFUTED.

F146 holds up but doesn't matter much. withMarket gives the two market-only players (Тамар Бэйтс and Алекс Адетокумбо, both at price 1000) a per-game figure from their price peers (7.04), but games=null, so playRate falls back to 0.85. That gives 68.0 season games and 479 points, against the median of their 176 price peers at 1000±100: share 0.618, 49.6 games, 345 points. That is +39%, but they still rank only 33-34 of 178 players at the minimum price (the top ones are at 580-800), so the advice would never pick them. The in-season update also corrects this fast, because their club calendar keeps counting. The per-game figure comes from price peers while the games figure comes from a generic default, which is inconsistent, and it is cheap to make both use the peers.

Drew Timme: the database has team PHX but Sports.ru club Миннесота, and the live Sports.ru snapshot also says Миннесота. Both clubs have full 82-game calendars, and he is forecast for 33 games at 6.4 FP/g. The effect is negligible, and the Sports.ru club is the right one for the club-limit rule. No change needed.

  - Clark (#53): 196, 151, 88.

- At 374 FP Sorber would rank only 8th among free-agent rookies (Acuff 826, Brown 687, Flemings 641 ... Mara 424, Swain 374).

The routing is a modelling choice, not a league rule, so the owner does not need to decide.

inseason-rate-low.reasoning:
This verdict covers four related findings. F097, the main bias, is CONFIRMED and holds up in both backtest pairs. F098 is REFUTED as material: the mechanism is real, but my rerun shows no held-out gain. F102 is real but negligible. F104 is a real test gap of low severity.

F097: I reproduced the production weights (est 20,5,20; new 30,2,5) with the repo's own point_cases and split functions.
- Signed error in the held-out pair 2024/25->2025/26, established players, by games played: n0 +0.14, n5 -0.30, n8 -0.35, n12 -0.33, n16 -0.41, n20 -0.32, n30 -0.48, n40 -0.44. Overall bias -0.254; n>=5 bias -0.372.
- The fit pair shows the same pattern (n>=5 bias -0.414). Newcomers are far worse: n>=5 bias -1.60 held-out.
- The bias does not come from the weak backtest prior. I replaced the prior with each player's own full-season mean, which is unbiased by construction. The estimate is still -0.35..-0.40 low at n>=5 held-out (-0.5..-0.6 in the fit pair), and newcomers are -1.17 low.
- Mechanism: a player's first games run below his own season level. Games 1-5 are -1.2..-1.4 FP and -1.7..-2.1 min; games 6-10 are -0.3..-0.5 FP; games 21+ are +0.27 FP. All three seasons show this, in any calendar month. Late-season games add about +0.3..+0.6 FP. So the update pulls the estimate down by about 0.25-0.4 against the prior, while the rest-of-season target sits 0.05-0.36 above the season mean.
- inseason_calibration.py picks weights on MAE alone and reports only MAE. data/inseason-calibration.json has no bias or RMSE field, so the bias is hidden from the published calibration and from the CI --check.
- A fix works without hurting MAE. I fitted an offset by games played on the fit pair, using the unbiased prior so it captures only the update's shift. Held-out results:
  - Established: bias -0.254 -> +0.162 (it overshoots because the shift varies by season, 0.5 in the fit pair vs 0.35 held-out); RMSE 2.8986 -> 2.8869; MAE 2.2833 -> 2.2879 (gain CI [-0.040, 0.031]).
  - Newcomers: bias -1.488 -> -0.268; MAE 2.6762 -> 2.4962; RMSE 3.5275 -> 3.2083.
  - A plain correction by checkpoint, fitted against the backtest prior: established bias 0.001, MAE 2.2792. It is cleaner on the numbers, but it partly absorbs the backtest prior's own bias.

F098: the participation bonus (+2 at 10+ min, else +1) is a step, but the rate x minutes form scales it with minutes. That part is true by construction. I built a participation-aware split and selected it on the fit pair (best 30,3,20, pg=20). Held-out MAE went 2.2833 -> 2.2840, gain CI [-0.016, 0.015]: no benefit. The auditor's best claim is also only 0.014 FP/game, so it is immaterial.

F102: all 874 players in the deployed default-draft.json have forecast.minutes. Only the 2 withMarket SPORTS_PRICE_PRIOR players (Alex Antetokounmpo and Tamar Bates, price 1000, prior 7.04) lack it. Those two go through the PRIOR_GAMES=10 fallback, so the newcomer('SPORTS_PRICE_PRIOR') branch can never be reached. Example: after 5 games of 30 FP at 34:00, the fallback gives 14.69 vs 13.71 on the newcomer path. The auditor's own MAE difference between k=3 and k=10 is 0.015. Negligible.

F104: JS perGame equals Python split to 2.1e-14 over 200 random cases. No test ties the two together: test_inseason_calibration.py and season.test.js each test their own side, and the JS 'calibrated update' test only re-reads the JSON. The gap is real but low severity.

No league rule is involved; these are modelling choices.

inseason-rate-low.userImpact:
Nothing is affected today (20.10, no games played yet). The bias starts within the first week of the season.
- **Established players:** once a player has 5-40 games, his FP/game estimate runs about 0.3-0.5 low (about 1.5-2% of a 20-25 FP/game player). Against a player with 0 games (back from injury, new signing), that is about 15-25 FP over ~50 remaining games. transferVerdict's threshold is 15 FP, so such a comparison can tip.

draft-illegal-after-price.reasoning:
The mechanism is real. installDatabase (src/database.js:9) copies the new catalog's price, priceStatus and, when positionAuthority is Sports.ru, the positions onto every picked player. enforceBudget (src/budget.js:5-10) then replays all 80 picks through pick() at those new values. A team that drafted legally can then fail the cap or the position check. The state gets pricingIssue, and validateCompletedRoster (src/simulation.js:156-157) throws. main.js:401 swallows the error into standings=null, and the note reads 'по 0 сценариям'.

The trigger is not present in production, though:
(1) The draft catalog is frozen. apply_sports_prices.py, collect_sports_current.py and collect_sports_fantasy_history.py all hardcode data/sports-prices-2026-10-17.json. The daily pages.yml rebuild reapplies the same file. Live in-season Sports.ru prices go only to sports-current.json, which the season module reads; installDatabase never reads them.
(2) The live snapshot of 20.10 shows 0 price differences and 0 position differences against the catalog for all 481 matched players.
(3) The season tab works from DRAFT_PICKS, not from the LIVE draft state in localStorage. Only the draft tab's preseason standings table and its warning are affected.

So the defect needs one of two things: a deliberate developer change that swaps in a new dated catalog, or a rare data event. In the second case, one of the 8 drafted ESPN-only rookies drops off every ESPN roster. I reproduced that case: the app gets pricingIssue 'Цена не подтверждена… Отмени пики', but the standings still compute.

Repricing pinned picks is intended and tested in tests/budget.test.js (legacy migration from unpriced data and from Yahoo positions). It was designed for in-progress, pre-draft migrations, not for a completed real draft. No league-rule decision is needed: the cap is charged at transaction time, and the draft is a recorded fact.

holdout-selection.reasoning:
The process claim is true, but the impact claim is not.

**The 2025/26 season was looked at during selection.** The FRAILTY grid in the comment at scripts/availability_model.py:22-25 (1: -2.702, 1.5: -2.667, 2.5: -2.653, 4: -2.660) matches my forward log score pooled over 2021-2026 to the third decimal (-2.7019, -2.6664, -2.6528, -2.6599). So 2026 was inside the selection data, and "Test: 2025-26 (untouched)" (projection_model.py:15, README.md:9) is not literally accurate. The other looks at 2026 the finder cites are also real, per the code comments and ACCEPTANCE:149:
- the share-regression choice, "forward-tested 2020-2026";
- the rejected minutes-dependent shrink target, "lost on the held-out season";
- the rejected team-minute scaling.

**Selection only biases a reported number when a clean selection on seasons up to 2025 would have picked something else.** I re-ran each fork that can be reproduced, and none of them makes the headline optimistic:
1. **FRAILTY.** Forward on 2021-2025 only, shape 2.5 still wins (-2.6406, against -2.6448 for 4, -2.6561 for 1.5 and -2.6926 for 1). Same pick, so gamesCoverage80 (0.798) and shortSeasonBrier (0.1325) carry no selection bias.
2. **Decay 0.6 and the 2400/640 priors.** The score is flat across the alternatives I tried (decay 0.4/0.8, priors 20/5 and 45/12): log score varies by less than 0.0006. On 2026, games coverage stays within 0.798-0.800 and Brier stays 0.1325. Negligible.
3. **The chain cannot move pairedGain95 at all.** evaluate() takes the centre as rate*share*n, so the chain only supplies the games pmf.
4. **Share regression vs shrinkage.** Forward 2020-2025, the regression still wins: games MAE 15.00 vs 15.01, season MAE 228.2 vs 229.2. Same choice on clean data, so no realised bias. On 2026 the regression gives 249.7 and gain95 [13.6, 36.7]; the shrinkage gives 254.4 and [8.8, 31.3].
5. **Minutes-dependent prior.** This is my own rough version (prior linear in past minutes per game); the owner's version is unknown. It beats the baseline in every forward season 2020-2025: per-game MAE 2.391 to 2.266, season MAE 228.2 to 221.3. On 2026 it wins season MAE (247.4 vs 249.7, gain [16.2, 38.8]) but loses per-game MAE (2.541 vs 2.532). If the owner's version behaved the same, a clean selection would have adopted it, and the published season MAE and gain would be slightly better than reported, not worse. Only per-game MAE would be optimistic, by 0.009 (0.4%).
6. **Team-minute scaling.** Not reproducible without its spec. It was rejected, so the reported number is the baseline's.
7. **Coverage80.** The conformal scales and neighbour pool use 2020-2025 only. The 0.746 already misses its 80% target and is disclosed (ACCEPTANCE:156). An earlier verifier showed 2026 is an unusually low season, not an inflated one.

**Net.** The defect is the "untouched" wording and the undocumented use of 2026 in the comments. The claimed optimism of pairedGain95, coverage and Brier comes out at about zero. The holdout report is not rendered in the UI: projection-model-audit.json is only published as a data file, and its figures appear in README and ACCEPTANCE text.

package-club-swap.reasoning: bestPackage (src/season.js:290) caps each club at max(CLUB_LIMIT, current roster count). When a team already has 3 players of one club, the LP can sell one of them and buy another player of the same club, so the team still has 3. clubRoom() (season.js:210), which every single swap, bestSwapFor and acquisition's swap path go through, refuses that purchase because two players of the club stay on the roster. ACCEPTANCE.md:107 says 'no purchase adds to it'. The package path therefore contradicts both the single-swap path and the documented rule, and the team stays in breach under checkRules (rules.js:96). The post-check at season.js:297 uses the same max() and does not catch it. No FBL roster has 3 players of one club today (max 2 for every team in live-sports-current.json), so the defect only appears after an NBA trade.

chain-anchor-degenerate.reasoning: Code path: projection_model.forecast sets games = ESPN games (the owner's call) and then calls with_games(p, chain, pid, TARGET, games, healthy). That makes Availability.distribution bisect the hazard scale c in [e^-6, e^6] until the chain's mean equals ESPN's number. A mean of 82 out of 82 is only possible with zero hazards, so c drops to e^-6 and the pmf becomes a point mass at 82. Targets of 77-81 push c to 0.1-0.25 and squeeze the lower tail. When the start state is not healthy, the target cannot be reached even at e^-6, and the pmf mean quietly stays below the published games. ACCEPTANCE line 155 documents "the hazards are scaled so the chain's mean equals the forecast games (regression, or its mean with ESPN)". The only validation it cites (80% games range covers 79.6% on 2025/26) used regression-anchored means. The ESPN-alone anchor in production was never validated. I reproduced every number the auditor gave, and my holdout shows the ranges fail badly in exactly this regime. The cause is the high target, not the chain's shape: anchored to the group's correct mean, the same chain is close to calibrated. Two parts of the claim are weaker than stated. (1) The "about 0% short-season risk" part does not matter: these players really are under a quarter of games only 0-6% of the time, and the warning needs 20%. (2) Means and rankings (games, meanSeason, projectedFP) do not change, and the draft (18.10) is over. What still matters today: the 80% games ranges shown on player cards, the season floor and ceiling widths, the in-season transfer confidence (pointsSpread uses (ceiling-floor)/mean), and the "Узкий разброс" (narrow spread) labels. These touch about 40 ESPN players, 5 of them fully degenerate. The in-season chainCurve rescales hazards to the in-season share (by up to e^6), so expected games during the season are not affected. The fix does not change the owner's call: published games stay ESPN's, and only the pmf's anchor changes. The fix also brings the code back in line with the documented "its mean with ESPN" method.

chain-anchor-degenerate.userImpact:
The draft is over, so what matters now is during the season.

- **Player card:** for Bridges, Champagnie and Carrington it says "С вероятностью 80% сыграет 82–82 матчей" ("80% chance he plays 82–82 games"). In reality, players who played 82 games come back with 82 again about 1 time in 5, and play fewer than 72 about 1 time in 3.
- **Other ESPN 77-81 players:** cards show lower bounds of 69-72 games. Our holdout puts the realistic bound around 55-57.
- **Season floors:** about 20-25% of the mean too high for the roughly 19 players ESPN projects for 77+ games. For example, Bridges' floor is 1026 FP against a 1265 mean (ratio 0.77); with a calibrated games distribution, players in that range sit nearer 0.55-0.65.
- **Transfer confidence:** for moves involving these players over the 4-week and season horizons it is overstated. The season spread is about 0.19-0.22 against the 0.25-0.30 that a realistic games distribution gives, which inflates z-scores by roughly 1.3x. That can push a borderline move over the 70% "advise" line.
- **Labels:** these players are more likely to get the "Узкий разброс" (narrow spread) label.
- **Short-season warning:** in practice unaffected; the real risk is 0-6%, and the warning needs 20%.
- **Unchanged:** per-game values, expected games, meanSeason and rankings.
- **Podziemski and Knueppel:** their pmf mean is 1.2-2.2 games below the published games.
chain-anchor-degenerate.fixPlan:
In scripts/projection_model.py, inside forecast() (around lines 587-589), keep the published games = espn['games'] as the mean (the owner's call is unchanged), but anchor the absence-chain pmf to a shrunk target instead of ESPN's raw number:

  pmf_games = (games + model_games) / 2 if espn else model_games
  if x: with_games(p, chain, pid, TARGET, pmf_games, healthy)

- Here model_games is the regression games after the healthy-start shift. That brings the code back to the documented "regression, or its mean with ESPN" method in ACCEPTANCE line 155.
- On the pooled 2024-2026 proxy holdout, w = 0.5 restores 80% coverage to 75-78% (from 24-45%) and the log score to -3.5/-3.8 (from -5.0/-5.7).
- It also makes Podziemski's and Knueppel's targets reachable.
- Everything downstream of the pmf then follows automatically: gamesRange, gamesMedian, shortSeasonRisk, the Ranges.games scenarios inside ranges.interval, and replacedGames. The interval's centre stays rate*ESPN games/82.

chain-anchor-degenerate.reasoning:
The core math holds. apply() sets games = ESPN games (the owner's call, PR #61, 22a494a, 20.10) and calls with_games(p,chain,...,games,healthy). Availability.distribution then bisects the hazard scale c over [exp(-6), exp(6)] until the pmf mean equals that target. When the target equals the season length L=82, the only distribution that can have mean L is a point mass at L, so the degenerate range is forced, not a numerical quirk. c hits the exp(-6)=0.0025 floor and the pmf puts 98% on 82. Targets of 77-81 force c to about 0.03-0.2, which takes out most of the spread.

ESPN's number is a point projection, and nothing calibrates it as a mean or a ceiling: there is no archive of ESPN projections, and the holdout coverage of 79.6% only covers regression-anchored pmfs, never ESPN-anchored ones. So the published 80% ranges for high-ESPN players are not validated. An empirical proxy shows they are far too narrow. Among healthy starters (played the club opener) who had 80+ games the season before (n=86), the next season had mean 71.3, q10 51, P(82) 16%. With 80+ games in both previous seasons (n=16): mean 77.4, q10 65, P(82) 44%. The chain anchored at ESPN 82 gives q10 82 and P(82) 0.98. Even Bridges (82 games in 5 straight seasons) does not justify 98%. Champagnie (17/74/80/82) and Carrington (81/82) clearly do not.

The owner's decision covers the point estimate only (it was made so the assistant stops selling healthy stars), not the range shape. So decoupling the pmf shape from the published games is a calibration fix, not a rule change. The pre-#61 anchor (model+ESPN)/2 is still described in ACCEPTANCE line 155 ("regression, or its mean with ESPN"). It gives q10 of 66 (Bridges) and 56-61 (ESPN-77 players), close to the empirical proxy.

Several parts of the finding are overstated:
- shortSeasonRisk near 0 is about right. The empirical P(<21 games) is 0-1.2%, and the UI warning fires at 20%, so no warning is lost under any anchor.
- The unattainable-target case (Podziemski 79 and Knueppel 78 giving pmf mean 76.8) is a 1-2 game gap that errs on the conservative side.
- The auditor's proposed fix "w fitted by log score of actual games" is impossible, because no ESPN archive exists.
- The decision impact is small. The draft is over, the in-season chainCurve re-fits the hazards to the in-season share anyway, and the confidence effect is under 1 pp.

What is left is materially miscalibrated displayed probability claims for a defined group: about 30 players, 9 of them on FBL rosters. Medium, not high.

(1) Every team is told to buy the same few players: CONFIRMED. I copied the UI's recommendation() logic: bestPackage for k=1..3 with protectSeason, the confidence filter, the transfers-left filter and the 15 FP-per-extra-move rule. I ran it for all 8 teams on the current deployed data (default-draft.json from f5c0328, live-sports-current.json collectedAt 2026-10-20T14:49Z, Sports.ru banks, transfersLeft=3).

(2) The page acts on stale rosters: CONFIRMED in the code and the cache headers.
- `taken` is ctx.rosters.flat() from load time. Live data comes from raw.githubusercontent, which serves `cache-control: max-age=300`. Adding a query string does not bypass that cache: I got x-cache HIT, source-age 39 s, on a fresh `?v=`.
