- So a GM acting on data older than about 1–6 minutes plus however long the page sat open can buy a player a rival just took. rules.js then flags it as a certain 'duplicate' breach (league-rules sharedPlayers, owner 20.10: "direct breach").
- This is a race. I did not observe an actual event, but the code supports it.
- Sub-claim "taken comes only from the journal": real but minor. allTransfers already cross-checks against live.teams[*].roster and warns on any difference. Today there is no difference for any team (0 warnings).

(3) Releasing a player hands rivals a big gain: REFUTED as measured. The auditor's "+269 to team 7" is the gross gain of the swap over the rival's own sold player, not the rival's gain over what it could already do. I measured each rival's best single swap before and after each team's recommended package (bought players removed from the pool, released players added).
- 4-week horizon: the largest rival increase is +61 season FP (team 2's releases, rival 5). It is +27 in two cases and 0 in all others.
- Season horizon: 0 in every case.

Owner exposure today is low. Team 0's recommendation (Randle→Zion) appears in only 1 of 8 packages, and at the season horizon the advice is HOLD. That is why the severity is medium, not high.

The site is public with a team selector, so whether rivals use it is unknown. The race exists anyway, because the same obvious free agents are the targets either way.

There are three sub-claims, and they come out differently.

(A) Same targets for every team, plus no re-check before the action. REAL. I copied recommendation() from season-ui.js: k=1..3, the confidence filter, season>=0, and the 15-FP-per-extra-move rule. I ran it on the current public/data/default-draft.json, the live season-live snapshot (collectedAt 2026-10-20T14:49Z), today=2026-10-20 and the UI default horizon 'month'. Tyler Herro is in the 'Сделай' package of 6 of 8 teams. Dyson Daniels is in 4, Trae Young in 3, and Zion Williamson, Saddiq Bey and Joel Embiid in 2 each. Nothing re-checks before takeAction. It is only a link to the team's Sports.ru page, and the season view polls only ESPN games (liveTimer), never sports-current.json. data/league-rules.json sharedPlayers says it is the owner's rule that the later buyer is in breach, and Sports.ru does not block the purchase.

The window is narrower than the finding suggests. The watcher reads the journals every 60 s and publishes on every change (season_watch.py). The page re-fetches on tab switch and visibilitychange. What stays open is the watcher lag plus the raw.githubusercontent CDN cache (up to about 5 min), plus any time a page sits visible without a refresh. The league feed posts a uniqueness check for every deal within about a minute, so a breach is caught fast. A collision needs two GMs following the site within those minutes. That cannot be verified, but it is most likely today, the last free pre-season day, which ends 20.10 21:30. The cost is a rules breach and an undo, which uses one of the 3 weekly transfers after 21:30, and the league is strict (team 7 is on the watchlist).

Recommending the same best free agent to several teams is not a modelling error in itself. Each team's advice is correct on its own, and any capable GM would find Herro. Mixed or assigned strategies would be wrong for a tool whose primary user is team 0 ('моя').

(B) 'taken' comes only from the journal rosters. IMMATERIAL on current data. allTransfers gives 0 warnings. No player in any live.teams[*].roster is missing from the derived rosters. allTransfers already warns 'Состав по журналу расходится' when the two disagree. It is a cheap robustness gap, nothing more.

(C) The externality ('a sale gives me +8 and a rival +269'). REFUTED as a measurement error. The auditor measured the rival's gross gain from the released player over the rival's own weakest slot (bestSwapFor). The right measure is the marginal gain: the rival's best package with the released players minus its best package without them. With k=1 and k=3, month horizon, on the current data, the largest marginal gain to any single rival is 17.2 FP over the month (team 1 releasing Deni Avdija). The others are 0.3 to 16.4, and 5 of 8 teams' packages give 0. The sellers' own gains are +71 to +140. The free pool in an 8x10 league is deep, so released players are almost always replaceable. A competitive penalty term would add solver cost and noise for a second-order effect. Keeping the own-FP objective is sound for a total-points league.

rookie-ranges.reasoning:
Facts that hold. Rookie.interval (scripts/projection_model.py:244-249) applies one pooled set of residuals to every rookie, with no conditioning on pick. In production that set is Rookie(2024 class).errors(2025 class): 113 rows, 108 of them with a rate. I recomputed the deployed ranges exactly, for example AJ Dybantsa 332/1104/2319, Boozer 318/1056/2218 and Peterson 289/942/1973. Ceilings run 2.10x the mean for the ESPN-combined rookies and 2.38-2.53x for picks 12-30. Dybantsa's P90 of 2319 sits above SGA's mean of 2218, and the best first season in the data is Wembanyama's 1652.

What fails. (1) The claimed mechanism, undrafted residuals inflating top-pick ceilings, is mostly wrong. Picks 1-14 have their own relative-error p90 of +0.78 (undrafted +1.44, all players +1.28). Taking the 20 nearest picks in log(pick) instead of the pooled set moves Dybantsa's ceiling only from 2318 to 2185 (-6%), and every top pick stays near 2.0x. (2) The auditor's statement that the residuals come from the same class they describe is false. The residuals come from the 2024-class fit applied to the 2025 class, so they are one class out of sample. What is missing is a coverage check on a third class; the report checks only point MAE. (3) Under-coverage for drafted players, which I measured at 0.59-0.86, sits almost entirely in picks 31-60 (coverage 0.36-0.82, mostly second-rounders who never played and fall below the floor). That group is irrelevant to FBL rosters. (4) All 8 rookies on FBL rosters are top-11 picks: Dybantsa, Peterson, Boozer, Wilson, Wagler, Morez Johnson, Burries and Lendeborg. For picks 1-14, my three-class rotations cover 37 of 42 seasons (88%), with 3 of 42 above the ceiling (7%, nominal 10%) and 2 of 42 below the floor. So the relevant ranges are not shown to be miscalibrated; if anything they are slightly wide. (5) The proposed fix, k-nearest residuals, does not help. rookie-ranges.reasoning:
The core claim holds. In scripts/projection_model.py:548, production sets rookies.residuals = Rookie(rookie_fit).errors(rookie_test).residuals. That is one pool of 113 relative rate errors (108 with a rate) from the 2025 class. Rookie.interval (lines 244-249) applies the same pool to every rookie, whatever his pick, and never removes the pool's median. Relative errors depend strongly on the predicted level:
- undrafted players (pred ~4.6 FP/G, n=54): p90 +1.44
- picks 31-60 (n=29): p90 +0.87
- picks 15-30 (n=16): p90 +0.32
- picks 1-14 (n=14): p90 +0.69 to +0.80

Multiplying a #1 pick's ESPN-blended 15.3 FP/G by (1+1.28) gives a 90th-percentile season of 2319 for Dybantsa, which is 32.2 FP/G over 72 games. That is 40% above the best first season in the data: Wembanyama, 23.3 FP/G, 1652 points. Flagg managed 1384 and Knueppel 1351. Back-of-envelope seasons for #1 picks since 2015 (Towns ~1750, Simmons ~1610, Ayton ~1420) all fall short of it too. Ceiling/mean is about 2.1x for drafted rookies and 2.4-2.5x for later picks. Veterans at the same level sit around 1.35x. So the top-pick ceilings are implausible, and that is a genuine math error: level-dependent relative errors were pooled, and the class-level shift was not removed (the 2025 top-5 picks had a median error of +0.49 against the 2024-fit model).

Parts of the finding are wrong or overstated:
1. The residuals do not come from the class they describe. The model is fitted on the 2024 draft class, its errors are taken on the 2025 class, and they are applied to the 2026 class. What is missing is coverage validation, which SCORING_AUDIT.md:14 admits.
2. The three-class coverage numbers do not show the ceilings are too wide. In my backtests the pooled scheme's drafted coverage was 0.76 / 0.71 / 0.59 / 0.86. The shortfalls come from the 2023 class's late picks falling below the floor (low-tail misses of 0.34-0.61) and from the 2025 lottery beating the ceiling (21% above). With about 14 lottery picks per class, coverage cannot settle the top-pick tail.
3. The auditor's proposed fix (k nearest picks in log(pick)) did not calibrate better. Drafted coverage was 0.76/0.68/0.55/0.69 at k=20 and 0.85/0.73/0.55/0.69 at k=30 with median centring. It also still leaves Dybantsa at about 2019 (k=20) or 1835 (k=30).

The decisive evidence is therefore domain plausibility at the top end, not the coverage figures.

Materiality is limited because every mean is unchanged:
- meanSeason and the rankings do not move.
- The two-piece normal in simulation.js keeps the mean.
- riskAdjustedValue uses only the floor, and floors of about 0.3x are defensible for top picks given injury and zero-game risk (Zion 434, Cade 717, Holmgren 0).
- The draft is finished, so the draft-time uses (the "Агрессивный" label, the rookie-timing study) no longer drive decisions.

What remains live:
- (a) Displayed title odds for the official rosters (main.js:401). Capping rookie ceilings at 1.5x the mean moves them by up to 2.6 pp (team 1 27.9% to 30.5%, team 4 23.9% to 25.4%, team 8 7.6% to 6.1%).
- (b) In-season pointsSpread (season.js:371). rel = (ceiling-floor)/(2*Z90*mean) is 0.70 for top rookies against 0.30 for veterans at 12-20 FP/G. That understates the confidence for swaps that involve rookies and can push them below CONFIDENT = 0.7. It fades as games are played (sqrt(20/(20+played))).
- (c) Player cards show "Сильный сезон" of 2319, 2218 and 2122 for Dybantsa, Boozer and Wilson, under the label "проверенные на прошлых сезонах" (main.js:235). For rookies that label is not accurate.

This is not an owner decision: neither league-rules.json nor ACCEPTANCE chooses pooled residuals. ACCEPTANCE:120 only says the ranges use that class's out-of-sample errors, which is true. Real and visible, but it affects only spread-based outputs, so medium rather than high.

(1) The GTD branch never fires. I observed this directly. In src/season.js, injuryFactor returns 0.5 for a non-Out entry only when day<back. gtd-never-fires.reasoning:
The mechanism is real. injuryFactor (src/season.js:138-145) gives a day-to-day player 0.5 only for games where `day<back`. On the live data, ESPN sets returnDate for every Day-To-Day/GTD player to the US date of his next game, and the Sports.ru calendar is dated in Moscow time (evening games fall on US date + 1). So the first upcoming game is never before returnDate, the factor is 1, and expectedPoints then starts the healthy chain at about 0.9 for that game. The auditor's stated cause is only half right. Even with US dates the next game is on returnDate itself (day==back), so the branch would still be dead. The real error is a misreading of what ESPN's field means: for a D2D player, returnDate is the doubtful game itself. The unit test (season.test.js:83, returnDate two days after the game) uses a shape ESPN never produces, which is how the dead branch got past it.

The magnitude is overstated. The '2.5x' and '0.308 vs 0.793' figures come from all rotation players who missed their club's last game. That group includes long absences that ESPN lists as Out with a returnDate, and the app already scores those as 0 by design: ACCEPTANCE line 98 says 'the injury report is not a second penalty', and the line-160 backtest only covers players who played their last game. Those cases are not part of this bug. For D2D players, the realistic gap on the next game is about 0.93 vs 0.5-0.65, not 2.5x. Two more limits on impact. First, ESPN rolls a D2D player's returnDate forward every day, so fixing the factor also reduces each successive next game while the listing lasts. That covers most of the 'elapsed run' worry for D2D-listed players without a semi-Markov start state. Second, no 2026/27 games have been played yet, so the 'unreported absence' part has zero effect today. It is a documented scope limit; recommend it as a later improvement, guarded so it applies only when there is no Out entry. Uniform 0.5 is crude (Curry is 'expected to play', Knueppel has 'no timetable'), but it is the repo's own intended constant. This is not a league rule, so no owner decision is needed.

return-alerts.reasoning:
I checked all three sub-claims against the code at f5c0328 and against the live state on data/season-live.

(1) DTD counts as "soon". In src/season.js:347, injuredTargets sets `dayToDay = !/out|suspension/i.test(status) || fantasyStatus==='GTD'` and `soon = dayToDay || returnDate <= today+7`. So every Day-To-Day/GTD free agent that passes the season-only deal test (minGain 30, monthFloor -Infinity) gets a "🔜 скоро вернётся" message. A code comment says this is intended. No owner decision or ACCEPTANCE line backs it. There is also no test: the only test, tests/season.test.js:203, covers only status Out.

(2) No confidence gate. In scripts/notify-transfers.mjs:154-156 the soon message always reads "🎯 Тебе: можно брать", whatever explainSwap's confidence. The `back` path (line 151) and decide() both branch on CONFIDENT. ACCEPTANCE.md:142 says "Market alerts (app and Telegram) show only confident moves; 'забирай' needs 70%, otherwise the bot offers the move as not sure". The code comment at line 39 says "Only a package the model is sure of starts a new message". The soon alert is the one proactive message that skips both the CONFIDENT and the DOUBTFUL bar, though it does print the confidence word.

(3) Repeats. The dedup key is `${id}:${status}:${returnDate}`, so the same injury re-alerts whenever ESPN changes the status or the date. On 20.10, 47 of 54 DTD entries carry returnDate = tomorrow (10-21) and 3 carry today. That is not the club's next game date, so it is a placeholder that will roll forward. Tobias Harris was alerted twice on day one: 'Day-To-Day:2026-10-20', then 'Out:2026-10-23'.

The alerts were really delivered. state.returns is only persisted by report() after a successful send with secrets configured; otherwise the script writes back the previous state unchanged. So 19 "скоро вернётся" messages went out on 20.10, and 17 were DTD.

Something else made the burst larger: with a large mid-morning bank, the include-package gain (pack3, +900..1450 season) comes mostly from the package's other moves. That turns nearly every injured player into a "target". It is a separate acquisition-marginal finding, not this one. Not owner-dependent: this is alert hygiene and consistency with the documented 70/60 bars, not a league rule.

package-legs-verdict.reasoning:
I checked all three parts of F011 against the code at f5c0328 and the live 20.10 snapshot. Only scripts/notify-transfers.mjs (lines 111 and 123) calls transferVerdict; it runs it once for each pending journal row.

(a) Each leg gets its own message. Team 0's 08:11:29Z journal holds five rows with the same seenAt, and the notifier sends five separate 'Твой трансфер зафиксирован' messages. Two of them lead with '🤡 Ослабление' (Jokic→Embiid at −1275 season, Knueppel→Okongwu at −209). The real change is White→Sabonis, at +400 season / +76 over 4 weeks. The leg gains do add up to that net, so the arithmetic is right; the headlines are what mislead. The code already treats a day as one package elsewhere: the bank check in allTransfers says 'Sports.ru confirms a day's transfers as one package', and league-feed protocols cover a day's package. The notifier is the exception.

(b) The 'before' roster ignores the rest of the package. It is today's roster with only this leg's inId swapped back. Players bought in other legs therefore count as already owned, and players sold in other legs count as free. The bank is the bank after the whole package plus inPrice. In my synthetic test (team sells PG#1→#81 and PG#9→#82 the same day), the verdict for leg #1→#81 says 'Лучше было: P9' (season +388). P9 is the team's own player, sold in the same package. Judged alone, the same leg would suggest P82. In the real data, the White→Knueppel leg gets 1900 to spend, while the bank before the package was 500.

(c) The alternative is ranked on the wrong horizon. transferVerdict asks transferOptions for its default sort='month' and only requires best.gain.month > gain.month. The verdict, by contrast, puts the season first (ACCEPTANCE.md line 111). Real output today: 'Derrick White → Kon Knueppel: +207 сезон · +29 · 💪 Усиление | Лучше было за те же деньги: Tyler Herro (1700), +59 сезон · +36'. That alternative is 148 FP worse on the season. Also 'Sabonis → White −400/−76 | Лучше было: Alex Sarr −500/−68', which is 100 FP worse on the season. That is 2 of the 6 'Лучше было' lines produced today, and part (c) happens on every verdict, not only in packages.

Why severity is low rather than medium: this is retrospective commentary in the personal Telegram bot. bestPackage, the alerts and acquisition advice do not use it, and no roster advice changes. The chained case in (a) needs a player bought and sold on the same day, which will be rare once FBL's 3-per-week limit applies from tonight. Parts (b) and (c) will keep happening on ordinary in-season packages and single deals.

season-ending-regex.reasoning:
The defect is real, and I reproduced it on the current live ESPN snapshot. It goes deeper than the auditors said, but on today's data it changes no decision.

1) src/season.js:136. The seasonEnding regex /out for (the )?season|miss the (entire|rest of the|20\d\d-\d\d) season/ does not match these comments:
- 'will miss the remainder of the season' (Furphy: OUT, returnDate 2027-01-02)
- 'has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles' (Hukporti: OUT, 2027-10-01)
- 'suffered a season-ending Achilles tear' (Simmons)
- 'will miss the entirety of the 2026-27 season' (Oweh)
Simmons and Oweh are still caught because their fantasyStatus is OFS. Hukporti is caught because his return date is after the season.

2) Both auditors missed this part, and it is the decisive one. Fixing the regex alone does NOT fix Furphy. injuryFactor (src/season.js:141) does `if(seasonEnding(injury))return back&&day>=back?1:0`, so it still trusts an in-season placeholder returnDate. I forced Furphy's fantasyStatus to OFS and he still got 36.8 games / 258 FP. 2027-01-02 is the same ESPN placeholder date that Butler has.

3) The regex in F090's fix is unsafe. Its branch `miss the (entire )?(20\d\d-\d\d )?season` matches 'Bilodeau will miss the season opener' in the live feed. That would zero a sprained player due back on 24.10. A generic year group in '(rest|remainder) of the (20xx-yy )?season' would also match 'who missed the rest of the 2025-26 season'. That kind of wording appears for returning players such as Butler (status Out, 25.4 games / 526 FP).

Materiality: Furphy is a 1000-price white-list SG at 7.0 FP/game and is on no FBL roster. I checked every team, every roster player and the week/month/season sorts: he is never in a top-12 transferOptions list, never in a bestPackage (k=1..3, season), and injuredTargets is empty for all 8 teams. So today the only visible effects are a phantom season outlook of 36.8 games / 258 FP if someone searches for him, and an injury chip saying 'до ~02.01' instead of 'до конца сезона' (season-ui.js:102 checks only OFS). Later, a valuable player described with the same wording could be shown as an injured buy target or kept as a hold. That is why the severity is low rather than medium. No league rule is involved.

shared-player-both.reasoning:
The defect is real and I reproduced it. seasonRosters (src/season.js:40-50) lets a second FBL team buy a player another FBL team already holds. stints (season.js:52-58) gives each team its own stint, keyed by team and player. teamPoints (season.js:247-254), teamFact (season-ui.js:251-256) and playerFact (season-ui.js:257-261) then add every game of that player to both teams. The forecast double-counts too: standingsTable (season-ui.js:133-138), leaguePlace (season-ui.js:266-270) and teamKpis (season-ui.js:400) add the shared player's in-game points and rest-of-season expectation to every roster that contains him.

This conflicts with two stated rules. The league owner's rule in data/league-rules.json sharedPlayers says a player may be on only one FBL team and the later buyer is in breach. And the league scores on Yahoo, which mirrors rosters and cannot put one player on two teams of one league, so the real standings cannot credit the later buyer with him.

It is not an owner decision. ACCEPTANCE.md:194 says "Team points are counted per team and player", but that line was written by the developer in PR #75 when the breach rule was added; the owner only ruled that the purchase is a breach. tests/season.test.js:19-21 asserts separate stints, but stints() can stay as it is if crediting is done in a separate step.

When it can happen: there are no shared players today (live journal has 20 transfers, none shared, and none in the Sports.ru rosters). The recommender never proposes a held player (transferOptions excludes taken players), so it only happens when a manager buys one on Sports.ru. Sports.ru allows that, the market does not show FBL ownership, the journal parser now keeps such transfers on purpose, and the owner wrote a rule for exactly this case, so it is plausible. When it happens the rules tab flags it correctly, but the league table, place and forecast ignore that.

What the later buyer should score while the breach stands is unclear: zero in that slot, or the player he sold (if the Yahoo mirror never applied the purchase). The owner has to decide that.

rookie-training-rows.reasoning:
The data error is real. I rebuilt the rows by calling scripts/projection_model.py's own rookie_rows, league_seasons and Rookie functions. My rebuild of the original rows gives exactly the deployed rate and games for all 71 rookie-extrapolated players in public/data/default-draft.json.

What I observed in rookie_rows (projection_model.py:258-278):
(1) Name joins fail. Ron Holland (#5), Osasere Ighodaro (#40) and Cameron Christie (#46) are recorded as 0-game picks, then counted again as undrafted debutants under 'Ronald Holland II' (81 games), 'Oso Ighodaro' (61) and 'Cam Christie' (12). In the 2025 class, Yang Hansen (#16) gets 0 games and 'Hansen Yang' (43 games) is counted as undrafted.
(2) data/nba-drafts.json holds the HTML entities 'Nikola Topić' and 'Nikola Djurisić', so those names can never match.
(3) The 'earlier' set covers only the league files from 2023-24 on, and 'later' covers only draft years y-1..y. Because of that, 21 of the 72 'undrafted' rows in the fit class are really veterans or earlier picks (Lonzo Ball, Steven Adams, Yabusele, KPJ, Payton, Okafor and others). They average 27 games against 15.5 for true debutants. The test class has 4 such rows (DaRon Holmes II, Sharife Cooper, Keels, Chandler).

With corrected rows, the auditor's numbers reproduce exactly:
- undrafted share 0.208 -> 0.163 (17.1 -> 13.4 games, 88 -> 68 FP)
- pick 3 games 68.6 -> 72.3
- holdout share MAE 0.199 -> 0.174
- but holdout rate MAE gets slightly worse, 2.956 -> 3.025

Downstream impact is small. Rookie games come from ESPN whenever it exists, and the rate is a 50/50 blend with ESPN. Per-player season changes:
- 18 UNDRAFTED_ROOKIE_MODEL players: -20 FP (all fringe, priced at 1000 or unpriced)
- drafted no-ESPN picks 12-28: +6 to +11 FP (2-4%)
- ESPN-covered picks 1-9: -6 to -13 FP (about 1%)
- rookie ranges: pick 12 goes from 96-1011 to 121-1157
So the severity is low, not medium.

F062: the share line does clip pick 1 to 82 games in every class fit (actual #1 picks played 70-75). But the only #1 pick (Dybantsa) has ESPN games (72), so 82 appears only in the sources.model display line. The class-to-class swing in the rate slope is real: -3.17, -1.79 and -3.00, with SE about 0.5. Leave-one-class-out with the 2023 class added shows that pooling two classes is not uniformly better than one (rate MAE 2.497 vs 2.411, 2.704 vs 2.624, 2.949 vs 2.959). Capping share at 0.9 changes share MAE by about 0.001. That part is immaterial or unproven.

F073: league_seasons reads MM.SS minutes raw. This leaves the participation threshold and the stat product unchanged, so it is negligible.

Related observation (same root cause, production side): apply() takes a pick only when DRAFT_YEAR == TARGET-1. So Thomas Sorber (2025 #15, isRookie, 0 games in 2025-26, no ESPN) and Bogoljub Markovic (2025 #47) get the undrafted mean of 88 FP. The pick-15 prior would give about 374 FP.

Separately, Dybantsa's seasonCeiling of 2319 against a mean of 1104 comes from rookie relative-rate residuals pooled across all picks. That is outside this issue.

rookie-training-rows.userImpact:
Rookie forecasts on the board are biased, but only a little:
- The 18 undrafted-rookie-model players are overstated by about 20 FP per season (88 vs 68, +30%). All of them are fringe players at a price of 1000 or unpriced, so no roster decision is likely to change.
- Drafted rookies without ESPN projections (picks about 12-28) are understated by 6-11 FP per season (about 1.5-2 games, 2-4%).
- ESPN-covered top-9 picks are overstated by 6-13 FP (about 1%).
- Rookie season ranges shift by about 10-15% at the ends (pick 12 goes from 96-1011 to 121-1157).
- The rookie holdout share error is overstated (0.199 vs 0.174), and the ACCEPTANCE/limitations claim of 'complete draft classes' is not met.
- The #1 pick's model line shows 82 games instead of about 72, but in display only, because ESPN games are used.
- A larger single-player effect comes from the same logic in production: Thomas Sorber (2025 #15, rookie-eligible, no ESPN) is shown at 88 FP instead of about 370 FP under the pick-15 prior, which hides him as a rookie transfer option. Bogoljub Markovic (#47) is shown at 88 instead of about 175.

real-draft-not-seeded.reasoning:
The finding is accurate about the code. src/main.js never imports DRAFT_PICKS or DRAFT_DATE; only season.js and simulation.js do. The draft tab's LIVE state comes only from localStorage. readDraft() turns a missing 'fbl-draft' key into '' and restoreBudgetDraft('') throws, so it falls back to newDraft(). loadDatabase() then installs the 874-player catalog with 0 picks. With 0 picks the following happens:
- renderPlan does not hide .plan-section, since it hides only for n===80 or no players.
- The worker runs planAdvice on pick 1.
- #postdraft is hidden because !n.
- The draft desk stays open.
So on any device without a recorded LIVE draft (a new device, cleared storage, iOS Safari evicting storage), the draft tab shows a live "Твой пик: бери сейчас" plan for a draft that finished on 18.10. The official result, the projected standings and the Telegram/txt export never appear there.

Nothing in docs/ACCEPTANCE.md or README says this is intended. Settings says only "Пики хранятся только на этом устройстве", which describes pre-draft storage.

A fix is feasible today. Replaying all 80 DRAFT_PICKS through engine.pick on the deployed default-draft.json succeeds: all teams fit the cap, and team 2 is at exactly 20000. The compact-save round trip and the reinstall keep all 80 picks with no pricingIssue.

I rate it low, not medium:
- The season tab is the default after 18.10 when no tab is stored, and it reads DRAFT_PICKS directly. Rosters, points, team forecasts and transfers are all unaffected.
- No pending decision depends on the draft tab: the draft is over and transfers are made in the season tab.
- The harm is confusing, stale advice plus a missing draft summary. That summary is largely redundant with the season tab's team view.

A subtle aggravator: initSeasonTabs writes 'fbl-tab' on every start. Any device first opened on or before 18.10 MSK therefore keeps 'draft' as its stored tab and lands on the draft tab by default. If that device has no LIVE picks, it opens straight onto the stale plan.
